patternCategory.description: Decision group that owns the pattern (single canonical home; provenance and related_patterns carry cross-listings)

patternScope.description: Implementation scope: the kind of program part the decision is local to

language.description: Target language of an implementation entry ('generic' for language-neutral guidance)

supportLevel.description: How the language relates to the classic pattern structure: native = absorbed into syntax/stdlib, idiomatic = a simpler local idiom replaces the full form, library = provided by stdlib or dominant framework, manual = full structure must be hand-written, discouraged = language semantics fight it, prefer 'alternative'

paradigm.description: Programming paradigm the pattern's mechanics belong to

provenance.description: Source catalog the pattern originates from (gof = Gamma et al. 1994, eaa = Fowler PoEAA, eip = Hohpe & Woolf, ddd = Evans/Vernon, posa1-3 = Schmidt et al., security-patterns = Schumacher et al., plop = Pattern Languages of Program Design, language-idiom = e.g. More C++ Idioms, functional-catalog = functional pattern lexicons, smalltalk = Beck 1997, xunit-test-patterns = Meszaros, game-programming = Nystrom, modern = post-2010 web/cloud catalogs)

aliases.description: Alternative names (e.g. 'Policy' for Strategy, 'Cheshire Cat' for Pimpl, 'Borg' for shared-state singleton)

intent.description: One-sentence intent: what the pattern does and what problem it solves (GoF 'Intent' section; the primary queryable summary)

problem.description: Decision trigger: the concrete recurring problem that warrants this pattern (the catalog's 'Use when' column)

context.description: Problem context describing when this pattern is applicable

benefits.description: List of benefits this pattern provides

quality_attributes.description: Numeric 1-10 scores; the eight fixed scoring axes plus the four extended axes in use (observability, coupling, discoverability, type_safety). Axes beyond the eight are not used by the scoring formula; unknown axis names are rejected so typos cannot silently drop a score.

quality_attributes_note.description: Free-text note explaining the assigned quality_attributes scores (why a score is low or high)

performance_notes.description: Free-text note on measured or expected performance characteristics of this pattern

role.description: Participant name as used in the pattern's collaboration (e.g. Context, Strategy, Subject, Observer)

responsibility.description: What this participant is responsible for in the collaboration

notes.description: Free-text clarification for this participant (responsibility boundaries, what it must not do)

participants.description: Named roles in the pattern structure (GoF 'Participants' section); empty for single-construct idioms

suitable_scopes.description: Program scopes where this pattern works well

unsuitable_scopes.description: Program scopes where this pattern should be avoided

avoid_when.description: Situations when this pattern should be avoided (including simpler alternatives that suffice)

pitfalls.description: Record-level traps when applying the pattern, independent of the chosen language realization (per-language traps live in the language files; the generic realization's own pitfalls in <name>.generic.json)

language_files.description: V8 language-file map (docs/implementation-guide.md §2.3): declares ALL realization files that join to this record — the generic entry (<name>.generic.json) plus one file per concrete language. Keys are exactly the 14 language enum values (generic + the 13 concrete); values are file names relative to this record's directory (<name>.<language>.json, colocated siblings). Required for every record; the integrity checker rejects any language realization content inside the main record itself.

paradigm.description: Facet: paradigms this pattern's mechanics belong to (filter, not a second category)

provenance.description: Facet: source catalogs this pattern is documented in

related_patterns.description: Conceptually related patterns in the catalog (canonical kebab-case names, resolvable via get_design_pattern)

related_patterns_notes.description: Per-related-pattern distinction notes: key = related pattern name, value = how this pattern differs from or relates to it

anti_patterns.description: Common anti-patterns and misapplications to avoid

migration_from.description: Patterns commonly refactored from (e.g. singleton -> dependency injection)

design_principles.description: Core design principles for this pattern (SOLID, composition over inheritance, ...)

version_history.description: Record revision history, one entry per released record revision
